name: Can a small ADU kitchen still have an island?

mainEntity.name: When is a kitchen island realistic in a compact ADU, and when is it a mistake?
mainEntity.text: When is a kitchen island realistic in a compact ADU, and when is it a mistake?

acceptedAnswer.text: An island can be a great feature in a larger ADU, but in a small kitchen it is often more trouble than it is worth. The issue is not whether the island looks good; it is whether the room has enough clearance around it to open drawers, move comfortably, and avoid bottlenecks. In many compact ADUs, a peninsula or a movable cart provides much of the same benefit without blocking circulation. Islands also increase the amount of cabinetry, countertop, and electrical planning required, which can add cost and complexity. If the kitchen is in a studio layout, an island can sometimes help define the room, but only if the proportions are generous. The best test is whether the island improves daily use or simply fills space. For most small ADU kitchens, the answer is to prioritize openness and workflow first, then add an island only when the floor plan truly supports it.
acceptedAnswer.description: A small ADU kitchen can have an island only if the room has enough clearance for doors, drawers, and circulation on all sides. In many compact ADUs, a peninsula, cart, or extra counter run works better than a true island because it preserves usable walking space.
